- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch the reversal; increase forecast slope gently.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; apply sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% sentiment).
